pool.text: A population of bacteria follows a logistic growth model where \( P(t) \) is the population at time \( t \) (in hours). The differential equation governing the population growth is \( \frac{dP}{dt} = 0.05P \left( 1 - \frac{P}{1000} \right) \). If the initial population is \( P(0) = 200 \), use Euler's method with a step size of \( \Delta t = 1 \) hour to approximate the population after 1 hour, \( P(1) \).
pool.sol:
Euler's method approximates the next value \( P(t + \Delta t) \) using the formula \( P(t + \Delta t) \approx P(t) + \frac{dP}{dt} \Big|_{t} \cdot \Delta t \). We are given \( P(0) = 200 \) and \( \Delta t = 1 \). First, we find the rate of change at \( t=0 \):

\( \frac{dP}{dt} \Big|_{t=0} = 0.05 \cdot P(0) \left( 1 - \frac{P(0)}{1000} \right) \)
\( \frac{dP}{dt} \Big|_{t=0} = 0.05 \cdot 200 \left( 1 - \frac{200}{1000} \right) \)
\( \frac{dP}{dt} \Big|_{t=0} = 10 \left( 1 - 0.2 \right) \)
\( \frac{dP}{dt} \Big|_{t=0} = 10 \cdot 0.8 \)
\( \frac{dP}{dt} \Big|_{t=0} = 8 \)

Now, we use Euler's method to approximate \( P(1) \):

\( P(1) \approx P(0) + \frac{dP}{dt} \Big|_{t=0} \cdot \Delta t \)
\( P(1) \approx 200 + 8 \cdot 1 \)
\( P(1) \approx 208 \)

pool.text: A population of bacteria is modeled by the logistic differential equation \( \frac{dP}{dt} = kP(1 - \frac{P}{L}) \), where \( P(t) \) is the population at time \( t \) in hours, \( k \) is the growth rate constant, and \( L \) is the carrying capacity.  It is observed that \( \frac{dP}{dt} = 200 \) when \( P = 100 \), and the maximum growth rate occurs when \( P = 500 \). Find the carrying capacity \( L \) of this population.
pool.sol:
The logistic differential equation is given by \(  rac{dP}{dt} = kP(1 -  rac{P}{L}) \). The growth rate \(  rac{dP}{dt} \) is maximized when the population \( P \) is half of the carrying capacity \( L \). We are given that the maximum growth rate occurs when \( P = 500 \). Therefore, \( L/2 = 500 \), which implies \( L = 1000 \). 

We can also use the other piece of information to verify this. When \( P = 100 \), \(  rac{dP}{dt} = 200 \). Substituting \( P=100 \) and \( L=1000 \) into the differential equation: 
 \( 200 = k(100)(1 -  rac{100}{1000}) \) 
 \( 200 = 100k(1 - 0.1) \) 
 \( 200 = 100k(0.9) \) 
 \( 200 = 90k \) 
 \( k =  rac{200}{90} =  rac{20}{9} \). 

Now we check the maximum growth rate at \( P = L/2 = 1000/2 = 500 \) with \( k = 20/9 \) and \( L = 1000 \): 
 \(  rac{dP}{dt} =  rac{20}{9}(500)(1 -  rac{500}{1000}) \) 
 \(  rac{dP}{dt} =  rac{10000}{9}(1 - 0.5) \) 
 \(  rac{dP}{dt} =  rac{10000}{9}(0.5) \) 
 \(  rac{dP}{dt} =  rac{5000}{9} \). 
 This calculation confirms that our value of L = 1000 is correct, as the problem states that maximum growth rate occurs at P=500, and the differential of the logistic function is indeed maximized at P=L/2.
